reviews.summary: The flamethrower spec never produced a result: both `team-play test` runs (plain and --grep @live) failed with exit 1 after only progress lines and a 600 s timeout. The battle frames agree with the design (jet toward the cursor along the turret, no cone outline), but the numeric criteria (±2° turret match, 0.5 rad, cone_deg, 0.3 s release) were not observed by me.

The change is documentation only: DESIGN.md §26 and docs/oil-spin.svg/.png. The diff touches only those three files, with 62 insertions and 0 deletions, and the image and section text meet every criterion. No browser scenarios or battle frames were run, because nothing the game renders was changed.

The grep criterion and npm test are met, and both specs use the helper. I couldn't observe either desktop spec pass: both team-play runs hit the 600s limit with no results. The implementer also saw about 12.5 min of host-lock waiting, so the lock is the likely cause.

The task is a design deliverable (§27 in DESIGN.md plus two pictures), and I checked each acceptance item against the files and the two PNGs. The four zones, the forest in three states, the greyscale copies, the layer and test names and the drawing numbers are all present.
The new file is the only change in the diff. Every zone value I compared matches balance.json (arena_zones version 1), and the file covers the rest of the criteria and negative cases.

The docs-only task is met: DESIGN.md §28 and docs/physics-weapons.png cover all five weapons, both states in colour and greyscale, and both bonuses on the spot, arming and spreading. The named layers, drawing numbers and what the hit player sees are all given.

I could not play the pickups @live scenario. Both runs of team-play test timed out at 600 s with no test result, probably while waiting for the e2e host lock, which the implementer also reported waiting on for 7 to 17 min. The only checks I made were the empty `git diff --stat` and the dispatcher's passing npm test.

On the deployed host the flag is off (/api/flags returns {"turret":false}). The garage and a battle (railgun/shield) look and behave as before. The merged run's npm test exited 0 with the 200-car balance test green. I could not play the flag-on state (production has no TURRET_ENABLED), and my smoke e2e spec timed out after 600 s with no tests run.

I could not play the pickups scenario. Both runs of `team-play test` timed out after 600 s without a test result, most likely because they were waiting on the e2e host lock. The criteria are unverified, and the only evidence is the implementer's claim and the dispatcher's passing npm test.

The patched shots tool opens the game with ?test=1, runs --weapon cryo against the deployed host and writes all 7 frames; the guard test is in the green npm test. Several criteria rest on the implementer's report: the --render-test run, the local per-mode timings, the temp-file guard failure and the diff scope.

The five frames and the README exist, and the two frames I opened (cryo.png, tesla.png) match the README claims. The spec did not finish through team-play within 600 s, so the seeding, snapshot-assertion and local-pass criteria are unverified by me.

Neither live pickups run produced a result: both waited the full 600 s and were killed by the tool timeout, most likely stuck on the e2e host lock (the implementer saw the same 6–17 min waits). No criterion was observed, so I could not verify the change.

The change is repo-only and touches e2e infrastructure. The fix takes a guard file, re-checks staleness under it, and removes the lock by rename. The new 8-process test, real concurrent processes with an exclusive marker, passed in the dispatcher's npm test. I did not independently re-run the pre-fix failure; I judged it from the test's structure and the report's quote.

I could not verify the behaviour. Both the Playwright run (timed out after 600s) and the battle-frames script hung on the deployed host, and the server log showed only build output. The only evidence is the PROTOCOL.md version line and a dispatcher test run with 1 unrelated-looking failure.

I read all five committed 1280×720 frames and the README. They come from the game's own renderer and show cryo, napalm, tesla, wave_rocket and laser firing. I could not re-run the spec: `team-play test` on the deployed host timed out at 600 s, so the "spec passes" criterion has no observation of mine.

This repo-only task has no player-visible change. I checked the tracked report in the checkout against each acceptance criterion by reading it, and the dispatcher's `npm test` run (659/659) covers the new test. I did not rerun `sim:pickups` or play a battle, and I could not check the diff scope.

The client scenario passes on live in 11.9 s, but the live replay scenario timed out at 300 s in my run, so the claimed 214 s pass was not reproduced. Verdict is fail on the replay criterion; a re-run or a shorter live variant is needed.

I could not verify the forest-hiding criteria by play: the task forbids Playwright, no e2e spec covers forest hiding, and I cannot run the unit tests. Only the PROTOCOL.md version line (version 2) is confirmed, and the battle frames render normally with no forest on screen.

I could not run the new spec: `team-play test` against the deployed host timed out after 600 s with no test lines, and the spec is local-only (`?render=test` plus a local server). I only read the committed README and two of the five frames (cryo.png, tesla.png), which are real 1280×720 renderer frames taken mid-fire and match the README table.

The design document covers the three cases, gives one rule each for the dead player and for mines and oil, treats flicker as an owner variant, and lists server tests. The diff touches only the new file. It fails because the required developer task in proposed_tasks is absent.

I could not rerun the spec: team-play test of chassis-shots.spec.ts timed out at 600 s with exit 1 and no test lines, and the implementer reported the same host-lock waits. The committed frames show the wheels in the zoom crops for A2, B1 and W4, but the garage frames do not show the Chassis line, and C1 has no crop.

The 8 tracked PNGs exist and the four battle frames and four mini-maps look right on inspection. My own run of arena-shots.spec.ts against the live host timed out at 600 s with no per-test line, so the spec's in-view assertion is not confirmed by me.

DESIGN.md §18.8 and docs/chassis-battle-scale.png meet the acceptance. The section names what fails at about 50 px for A2, B1, C1 and W4, gives numbers scaled by r/23, shows a greyscale reading, states the r+0.5 limit with the hit circle and camera unchanged, and records a camera zoom only as an owner option. I could not run a git diff to confirm that only the four files changed; I relied on the implementer's file list.

Acceptance rests on 4 unit tests in forest-snapshot.test.ts, which passed in the dispatcher's full npm test run (exit 0), and PROTOCOL.md carries version 2 and the rule. No live two-client forest play was done, so live behaviour is unproven.

The design document is substantively good: it has one rule each for the dead player and for mines and oil, an owner variant for flicker with hidden_alpha at 0, and a per-rule server test list. It fails because the required single developer task in proposed_tasks, with checkable criteria, appears nowhere in the file or the report.

The 8 frames and the README are in the checkout, and the opened battle frames show hatched pillars and thin walls drawn by the game's own renderer. The spec timed out after 600s on the live host, so the in-view assertions and the local pass are unverified.

Repo-only Vitest task: I read the new test and the dispatcher's npm test run (97 files, 667 tests passed, exit 0). The test covers every acceptance criterion, with numbers read from balance.json and field names from PROTOCOL.md. I did not run the test or git diff --stat myself, and no browser play was in scope.

The change only adds report text, and the diff is limited to the allowed file. I could not watch client:44 pass myself, because the live run timed out after 600 s waiting for the host lock. The report's claims are therefore unverified by me.

The spec could not be played here: `team-play test` on chassis-shots.spec.ts timed out at 600 s without a result. The tracked frames and README look right by eye, and the dispatcher's npm test passed (669/669).
